name: async-queue-drain-becomes-method-bulk-html-loader
behavioral_change: In async v_new (3.0.0), the event-style members of `queue`, `priorityQueue`, `cargo` and `cargoQueue` such as `q.drain` changed from assignable properties to methods that register a callback, so `q.drain = fn` must become `q.drain(callback)`. async 3 defines these members as non-writable, so in sloppy-mode CommonJS code the old assignment is silently ignored: no exception, no warning, and the user's function is never registered.
downstream_effect: bulk-html-loader's `BulkHtmlLoader.prototype.load` signals completion of a batch of URL fetches through `q.drain`; after the upgrade the completion callback never fires and all six end-to-end mocha tests time out. The failures contain only mocha's timeout message and node-internal timer frames, with no production file, line number, or mention of drain, queue or the async library.
reference_fix: The reference fix changes one site in lib/BulkHtmlLoader.js, replacing `q.drain = function() { callback(null, that._queue); };` with `q.drain(function() { callback(null, that._queue); });`.
documented_in: The async CHANGELOG at https://github.com/caolan/async/blob/v3.2.6/CHANGELOG.md, v3.0.0 Breaking Changes section, announces the change and states the new form `q.drain(callback)` in the same entry, so the changelog itself shows the new code form.
failing_tests: HtmlLoader should produce two successful and one failed load
HtmlLoader should invoke onItemLoadComplete callback three times
HtmlLoader should invoke callbacks for onError, onWarning and onItemLoadComplete
